 Proposed changes to SNAP eligibility drop millions from benefits
 BY 
 Juliet Lemar
 Los Angeles 
 PUBLISHED 6:30 AM PT Nov. 16, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 6:30 AM PST Nov. 16, 2026 
 SHARE 
 LOS ANGELES — On Nov. 10, The Trump administration filed a new proposal to tighten Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program eligibility requirements to limit benefits for households with a gross income above 130% of the poverty line, or about $35,500 for a family of three, according to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities.
 Under the new rule, households above SNAP’s income thresholds would not qualify for food stamps if they receive non-cash TANF benefits, such as childcare assistance or job training.
